messages.subject: JSS paper and blavaan 0.3-2 released
messages.body_plain:
blavaan 0.3-2 has been released to coincide with publication of the blavaan paper in Journal of Statistical Software. The main user-visible change in 0.3-2 involves bug fixes for Stan, primarily dealing with missing data. Further details are here:

http://faculty.missouri.edu/~merklee/blavaan/version.html

The published blavaan paper is available here:

https://doi.org/10.18637/jss.v085.i04

Ed

messages.subject: convergence criteria
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I just came across the package blavaan. It's awesome. Thank you Edgar.

I am trying to use it for a simulation study in which I want to see whether Bayesian estimation would improve the convergence rate of some models compared to ML estimation. While it is easy to tell whether the model converged, it is more subjective in Bayesian context. I tried the following criteria. But I am not sure whether that is too stringent.

Basically, what I did is to see whether the largest PSRF in a model is greater 1.1. If it is, then I treated it as evidence of non-convergence. Is this a reasonable choice? Or do you have any better suggestion?

Additionally, I noted that with 500 observations and 13 variables, it took about 7 hours to finish 100 replications!! I know that Bayesian estimation is very slow. But is this within normal range?

Thanks a lot. Looking forward to your opinions.

Best,
Bo

messages.subject: Re: convergence criteria
messages.body_plain:
Bo,

I think the standard recommendation in the literature is to use a PSRF threshold of 1.05. blavaan starts throwing warnings/errors at a PSRF threshold of 1.2 (parameters' posterior means are often stable around this value), but I have found that the newest versions of JAGS and Stan get below 1.05 pretty quickly (for many models, at least). Also, parameters' posterior means tend to be more stable than likelihood values (that go into DIC/WAIC/etc), so I would not assume that the information criteria are stabilized just because the individual parameters have converged.

Regarding speed, that does seem slow. It partly depends on the model, but you might try Stan in addition to JAGS (or vice versa; see the target argument of blavaan). Also, there are some parallelization options that can be sent to JAGS or Stan via the bcontrol argument. Finally, there is also some parallelization built into blavaan that only works on mac/linux machines (for summarizing posterior samples). That parallelization could also theoretically be coded to work on windows, but I currently have no way to do testing on windows.

Best,
Ed

messages.subject: Re: convergence criteria
messages.body_plain:
I would recommend 1.05 because that value has been most established in the literature. Would also be worth looking at the effective sample size of each sampled parameter, which takes autocorrelation into account. (The label is "neff" in the blavaan output.)

Ed

messages.subject: Re: convergence criteria
messages.body_plain:
The first "diagnostic from parser" thing is harmless and is to be expected (for blavaan, at least). But the "rejecting initial value" thing might indicate a bug. You could try using the argument inits="prior" to see if that helps. I'd also be interested in seeing the model and data if it can be shared, to see if it is a bug. (Could send to my email if you want, as opposed to the whole group.)

Ed

messages.subject: Priors Regression Coefficients Mediation Sem
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I am new to both the forum as well as to (b)lavaan, but I have question considering the specification of priors of regression coefficients in a mediation SEM model I am working on specifying. I would like to specify different priors for gamma21, gamma11, and beta21 in the model specified below. I know that Blavaan (using Stan) uses as default normal(0,10) and that I can change that using the dpriors command, but how could I specify 3 different priors for the different regression coefficients? I have tried adding  prior("normal(0, 25)") as example in front of the regression coefficients, but when I check the output the default normal(0,10)  is still being used. I checked different tutorials and vignettes but cannot find anything about this type of prior specification.

modelSEMB4<- '
# measurement model
Future =~  X1 + prior("normal(0, 33)")* X2 + prior("normal(0, 33)")*X3
Studiousness =~ Y1 +  prior("normal(0, 33)")*Y2 +  prior("normal(0, 33)")*Y3
Academic =~ Y4 +  prior("normal(0, 33)")*Y5 +  prior("normal(0, 33)")*Y6

# direct effect
Academic ~ gamma21*Future
# mediator
Studiousness ~ gamma11*Future
Academic ~ beta21*Studiousness
# indirect effect (gamma11*beta21)
indirecteffect := gamma11*beta21
# total effect
total := gamma21 + (gamma11*beta21)'

mypriors<-dpriors(target="stan", nu="normal(0, 33)", itheta="gamma(.5,.5)", ipsi="gamma(.5,.5)")
bfitpstan4<-bsem(model=modelSEMB4, data = data, dp=mypriors,  n.chains = 2, burnin = 1000, sample=2000, target = "stan")

Best,
Laurent

messages.subject: Re: Priors Regression Coefficients Mediation Sem
messages.body_plain:
Laurent,

There are a couple ways to do this. If you want all regression weights to have the same prior, you could add "beta" to dpriors():

dpriors(target="stan", beta="normal(0,25)")

If you want to set each prior individually, you could do something like

Studiousness ~ prior("normal(0,25)")*Future + gamma11*Future

Ed
